hypothesis: Conditioning valid six-mark Golomb-ruler generation on an explicitly selected difference, then using scarce-currently-compatible differences as exact-cover anchors, will assemble more than four mutually disjoint rows and may find a scope-111 DTS where uniform global catalogs stall.
rationale: The uniform 250,000-row catalog reached only depth four and the baseline-local methods reached at most depth five. Both methods under-supply rows containing differences that become constrained after several selections. Difference-first generation changes the representation from uniform row sampling to on-demand allocation of scarce differences while retaining exact row-internal and cross-row compatibility checks.
expected_information_gain: Distinguishes whether the previous depth ceiling is caused by poor coverage of constrained differences or by genuine scarcity of compatible scope-111 Golomb rulers in this finite search family.
method: For each difference 1..111, generate up to 400 valid scope<=111 six-mark Golomb rulers conditional on containing that difference. Deduplicate by exact 1..111 difference mask. Build an inverted difference index and recursively select seven pairwise-disjoint row masks, probing the 24 statically rarest currently uncovered differences, branching on the one with fewest compatible rows, and allowing at most six omitted differences. Rank compatible rows by coverage of statically scarce uncovered differences. Use the independent integer DTS verifier on any complete assignment.
metric: catalog cardinality, valid conditional rows, exact-cover nodes, maximum assembled depth, omitted-difference count, target assignment, and independent DTS validity
metric_relation_to_true_objective: A complete seven-row assignment accepted by the independent integer validator is exactly a true-objective scope<=111 witness; catalog size and partial depth are finite-family diagnostics only and cannot establish infeasibility.

configuration.anchor_generation: conditional pair with exact difference anchor, then random completion and local Golomb validation
configuration.cover_branching: fewest currently compatible rows among statically rare uncovered differences plus six-gap budget

kill_condition: Stop at the first independently validated target witness, catalog/DFS completion, 120-second wall budget, or 2,000,000 search nodes. Do not infer global impossibility from finite catalog failure.

baseline_comparison.expected_relation: strict improvement only if complete and validator-valid

previous_best_comparison.expected_relation: new conditional-generation and scarcity-anchored exact-cover family

interpretation: A balanced catalog of 44,378 deduplicated rows generated conditional on one allocated difference reached exact-cover depth 5, matching the prior local-neighborhood ceiling, and produced no target assignment. This is finite-family evidence only.
what_was_learned: Single-anchor conditioning supplied all 111 differences evenly but did not increase compatible seven-row depth; the missing structure may require rows conditioned on multiple simultaneously scarce differences rather than more single-anchor coverage.
recommended_next_action: Test one multi-anchor row-allocation family, conditioning generated rulers on pairs of differences and retaining scarcity-aware exact-cover recursion; close the family if depth remains at five or lower.
repetition_justification: This is not a parameter sweep of the uniform catalog. It changes row generation itself by conditioning on allocated differences and changes the recursion to scarcity-aware on-demand compatibility branching.
